newsitem.title: THAILAND: Asia Times newspaper stops publishing temporarily.
newsitem.headline: Asia Times newspaper stops publishing temporarily.

text.p: Thai-owned regional newspaper Asia Times said on Thursday that it would stop publication temporarily because of financial difficulties.
"We have been told that as of Friday (June 27) we will cease to be published in paper form for a period of between 60 and 90 days for financial reasons," a senior editor at the paper told Reuters.
The English-language daily, which was launched last year and covers Asian business news mainly, is the flagship publication of the Manager Media Group Plc.

"We have funded Asia Times on our own for the last few years, but the conditions of the Thai economy are such that we are required to reevaluate the business side of Asia Times," publisher Sondhi Limthongkul said in a statement.

The internationally distributed paper would be redesigned and relaunched under a new publisher once its finances and business management were improved, the statement added. The closure comes as Thailand faces its worst economic downturn in more than a decade amid sharply slowing growth, high borrowing costs and falling profits which have seen many companies rationalise as they struggle to survive.

Staff at the newspaper, who have faced wage delays this year, said they were told at an afternoon meeting that the management would decide on redundancies in 10 days but were advised to begin looking for new jobs.
In March they were told that the paper's future was to be secured by a partial sale of one of the parent company's subsidiaries to overseas investors.
Sondhi has interests in communications and satellite industries through his International Engineering Plc and Asia Broadcasting and Communications Network.
It was not immediately clear if other publications owned by Manager Media Group including the pan-Asian English language magazine Asia Inc were affected.
